1. Purpose

This policy establishes consistent expectations for remote work while supporting effective operations, employee well-being, protection of company information, and compliance with applicable law.

2. Scope

This policy applies to employees authorized to work remotely, whether regularly, on a hybrid schedule, or occasionally. It supplements other company policies and any applicable employment agreement. Applicable law and binding agreements prevail if they conflict with this policy. Contractors are governed by their contracts unless expressly covered.

3. Definitions

  • Remote work: Approved work performed away from a company workplace using an approved location and appropriate technology.
  • Hybrid work: An arrangement combining remote work and work at a company workplace.
  • Approved work location: A location authorized for the employee’s remote work, including any applicable geographic restrictions.
  • Remote-work arrangement: The documented terms approved for an employee, including location, schedule, and any specific conditions.
  • Company information: Company or third-party information handled for work, whether digital, printed, or discussed verbally.

4. Eligibility

4.1 Assessment. Remote work is subject to approval based on factors such as job duties, service and collaboration needs, performance, information-security requirements, the proposed work location, and operational or legal considerations.

4.2 Requests and approval. Employees should submit a request to their manager with the proposed schedule and location. The manager will consult Human Resources and other teams as appropriate and communicate the decision and any conditions. Employees must not begin an ongoing arrangement until it is approved and documented.

4.3 Fair consideration. Eligibility decisions must be applied consistently and without unlawful discrimination. Requests for reasonable accommodation will be handled through the applicable accommodation process; this policy does not replace that process.

4.4 Review. Approval is not a guarantee of permanent remote work. Arrangements may be reviewed, changed, or ended based on business needs, performance, security, or legal requirements, subject to applicable law, agreements, and accommodation obligations. The company will provide notice when practicable.

5. Policy requirements

5.1 Work location and changes.

  1. Work from the approved location and maintain contact details with the company.
  2. Obtain approval before changing the regular work location or working from another state, province, or country; tax, employment, immigration, privacy, and security requirements may apply.
  3. Attend company workplaces, meetings, training, or business events when reasonably required and communicated.

5.2 Schedule, availability, and timekeeping.

  1. Follow the approved schedule, communicate availability, and respond through designated channels during working hours. Coordinate schedule changes with the manager.
  2. Record all hours worked accurately when required, take applicable meal and rest breaks, and obtain advance approval for overtime where required by company procedure. All time worked must be reported and will be paid as required by law, even if not approved in advance.
  3. Use established procedures for leave, absence, and reporting illness.

5.3 Performance and conduct.

  1. Meet the same performance, conduct, confidentiality, and service standards that apply on site; participate in required meetings and training.
  2. Maintain a workspace that allows employees to perform their duties without avoidable interruptions. Arrange dependent care as needed to meet work responsibilities.

5.4 Workspace and safety.

  1. Maintain a reasonably safe, suitable workspace, including appropriate seating, lighting, and a reliable connection. Follow applicable ergonomic and safety guidance.
  2. Promptly report work-related injuries, hazards, and equipment problems through company procedures. Any workspace assessment or access will be arranged with appropriate notice and in accordance with law and privacy requirements.

5.5 Expenses and disruptions.

  1. Obtain required approval for expenses and submit eligible expenses under company procedures. The company will reimburse expenses as required by law or applicable agreement.
  2. Promptly notify the manager of an outage or other disruption. The manager and employee will agree on appropriate alternatives, such as adjusted duties or another approved location.

6. Equipment and security requirements

6.1 Equipment.

  1. Use company-issued or expressly approved devices and software for company work. Follow IT instructions for setup, updates, maintenance, and support.
  2. Protect equipment from loss, damage, and unauthorized use; do not allow household members or other unauthorized persons to access company devices or accounts.
  3. Company equipment remains company property and must be returned as directed when the arrangement ends or employment terminates.

6.2 Access and data protection.

  1. Use unique passwords, multifactor authentication, screen locks, encryption, and approved remote-access tools where required by IT. Do not share credentials.
  2. Use a secure network and company-approved connection methods. Avoid public or shared networks unless using the security measures prescribed by IT.
  3. Store, share, and dispose of company information only through approved systems and methods. Do not send work information to personal accounts or use unapproved storage or applications.
  4. Prevent others from viewing or overhearing confidential information; secure printed materials and dispose of them according to company procedures.

6.3 Incident reporting and monitoring.

  1. Immediately report suspected phishing, unauthorized access, lost devices, or other security incidents to IT or the designated security contact; follow their instructions and do not conceal an incident.
  2. Company systems and devices may be monitored or managed for legitimate business and security purposes in accordance with applicable law and company notices.

7. Responsibilities

RoleResponsibilities
EmployeeFollow approved terms and company policies; maintain availability and a suitable workspace; record time accurately; protect information and equipment; promptly report issues and incidents.
ManagerAssess requests consistently; document and communicate approved terms; set expectations; monitor outcomes; coordinate changes and address reported issues.
Human ResourcesAdminister the policy; advise on eligibility, accommodations, employee relations, and applicable employment requirements; maintain relevant records.
IT / Information SecurityDefine technical requirements; provision and support approved tools; manage access; respond to security incidents and advise on secure practices.
Company leadershipProvide oversight and resources, and authorize policy updates as appropriate.

7.1 Questions and noncompliance. Direct policy questions to Human Resources and technical questions or incidents to IT. Violations may result in corrective action, including modification or termination of remote-work privileges or disciplinary action, subject to applicable law and company procedures.

8. Acknowledgement

I acknowledge that I have received and read the Employee Remote-Work Policy, understand that I am expected to comply with it, and know that I may direct questions to Human Resources. My signature acknowledges receipt and understanding; it does not by itself approve a remote-work arrangement or alter applicable legal rights or employment terms.
